status: Benchmark-only CPU attribution; no native generation change or default speedup claim.
implementation: Add one pre-batch RUSAGE_SELF sample, reuse the existing post-batch RSS sample, and add two Unix-clock reads around the measured batch. Report process user/system/total CPU, CPU per region, average scheduled cores, context switches and faults. No per-request clocks, counter hooks or generator changes. Unix timestamps align observations while original monotonic timing remains unchanged.
scope: Current-process/all-thread CPU counters bracket only the measured batch. Includes executor/host driver CPU, excludes warmups/readiness/snapshot/hash/NBT validation. Unix timestamps align observations, not latency. CPU seconds and concurrent/GPU durations are not wall-time shares. Classifier misses native processes and does not prove idle-machine conditions.

usage.clock_scope: Unix timestamps bracket the batch and CPU samples for observation alignment only; wall-clock adjustments may affect them. Latency uses the existing monotonic perf_counter interval. No per-request CPU attribution is implied.
usage.scope: RUSAGE_SELF deltas for the whole process and all its threads around the measured batch, including executor creation/join and host driver work. Excludes startup, warmups, readiness wait and later snapshot/hash/NBT validation work. GPU device execution and other processes are not CPU time here. Context-switch/fault counts are platform-reported observations, not wait durations. Average scheduled cores is CPU seconds divided by elapsed batch seconds, not worker occupancy or an elapsed-time share.

decision: CPU accounting is validated as additive benchmark metadata, not a native optimization or uncontended timing conclusion. Second-seed current CPU/region is 2.23–2.33 s serial versus 3.36–4.03 s with 8 callers, while Overworld is closer. Control CPU variation is large too. Cache/reconstruction work can vary with concurrent request completion and snapshot availability; this is a hypothesis to investigate, not proof of a specific cause.

next_candidate_review.finding: Reuse captures completed neighbor archives at job start and holds that immutable set through every root. Completed snapshots published during the request are not added.
next_candidate_review.status: Source reviewed. Existing bounded between-root refresh retains old owners, adds newly available unique neighbors with 8-entry/512 MiB bounds and uses try_lock. Not selected or rewritten in this cycle. A retest on current runtime needs full output and repeated whole-generation evidence; earlier source predates C199 live tile reuse.

limits: Process CPU includes all current-process threads and host driver work. It is not exclusive feature CPU, wait time, worker occupancy or a wall-time share. Some exact measured windows overlap classified tests; broader native/desktop activity remains. CPU time can also vary with frequency, contention and cache histories. No causal speedup or full concurrent acceptance.
reproduce: Use exact command arrays and retained libraries from validation-receipt.json with fresh output paths. CPU metadata survives unchanged in suite measurements. Preserve all current worlds, binaries, logs and worktrees; no test data was removed.
